title: South Central
body: Born in Los Angeles on April 13, 1979, and raised in South Central by his grandmother, Lela Nicholson. She is the one who pushed him toward the game.

title: Crossroads
body: At Crossroads School in Santa Monica he became the best high school player in the country: 1997 Gatorade National Player of the Year, California Mr. Basketball, first-team Parade All-American and a McDonald's All-American. As a senior he won the Beach Ball Classic in Myrtle Beach and took the MVP.

title: UCLA
body: He chose UCLA over Kansas, Georgia Tech and Duke so his family could watch him play. Pac-10 Freshman of the Year in 1998, then a torn ACL coming down from a dunk in the NCAA Tournament. He came back the next season first-team All-Pac-10 and an AP All-American, and went to the draft.

title: No. 3
body: The Charlotte Hornets took him third overall in the 1999 draft. He wore No. 1.

title: 89 feet
body: At the Bradley Center in Milwaukee, with 0.7 seconds left in the third quarter, he let it go from 89 feet. It went in.

title: All-Star
body: An All-Star in 2002 and again in 2004, the year he made All-NBA Third Team, won the Skills Challenge and led the league in steals.

title: Golden State
body: Traded from New Orleans to Golden State on February 24, 2005, and handed No. 5. The Warriors had missed the playoffs for a decade. Two years later Oakland would be on its feet.

title: One Shot
body: Reebok's short film One Shot, directed by Emmanuelle Chriqui, with Baron as Sam: roller skates, a boombox and an empty playground, in black and white.

title: 8 over 1
body: The Warriors beat the top-seeded Dallas Mavericks 4–2, the first No. 8 seed to beat a No. 1 since the first round went to seven games. He averaged 25 points in the series. Steve Kerr called it “outrageous… stunningly athletic and creative and explosive.” Oakland wore yellow: We Believe.

title: Over Kirilenko
body: Game 3 against Utah. He went up over Andrei Kirilenko, threw it down, and stood there flexing while the building shook. 32 points, and a 125–105 win.

title: Home
body: He opted out in Golden State and came home, signing with the Los Angeles Clippers on July 10, 2008.

title: Cleveland, New York
body: Traded to Cleveland in February 2011, then on to the Knicks that December, wearing 85. On May 6, 2012, in Game 4 against Miami, his knee gave out and he left the floor on a stretcher.

title: The Drew
body: Back on the court in South LA: 44 points in the Drew League in July 2015, and a documentary about it, The Drew: No Excuse, Just Produce. Then a D-League run with Delaware in 2016 and the BIG3 in 2018.

title: The builder
body: Verso Entertainment with his high school friend Cash Warren in 2005. 5 Balloons Interactive in 2012, whose first game was Getting Buckets. Black Santa Company in 2016, to tell African American stories. And a hand in producing Crips and Bloods: Made in America.

title: On air
body: A Players Only panelist on TNT from 2017. His own sitcom, WTF, Baron Davis, on Fuse in 2019. Dancing with the Stars in 2025, and Raiders: Talk of the Nation.

title: Now
body: Every one of these moments still plays somewhere online, scattered across other people's channels. History of the Game brings them back to one place and points every one of them back to him.
